indicators.flag: A customer with no history or background of using, exchanging, or otherwise interacting with virtual currency attempts to exchange a high amount of fiat currency from an existing or newly opened bank account for virtual currency or attempts to initiate high-value transfers to VASPs.
indicators.red_flag: No-VC-history customer → high-value fiat-to-VC / VASP transfer (out-of-pattern crypto onramp)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D7.

indicators.flag: A customer mentions or expresses interest in an investment opportunity leveraging virtual currency with significant returns that they were told about from a new contact who reached out to them unsolicited online or through text message.
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer mentions that they were instructed by an individual who recently contacted them to exchange fiat currency for virtual currency at a virtual currency kiosk and deposit the virtual currency at an address supplied by the individual.
indicators.red_flag: Third-party-directed VC-kiosk deposit to supplied address (scammer-controlled wallet)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer appears distressed or anxious to access funds to meet demands or the timeline of a virtual currency investment opportunity.
indicators.red_flag: Distressed/time-pressured fund access for VC investment (coerced-urgency victim)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer uncharacteristically liquidates savings accounts prior to maturation, such as a certificate of deposit, and then subsequently attempts to wire the liquidated fiat currency to a VASP or to exchange them for virtual currency.
indicators.red_flag: Early CD/savings liquidation → wire-to-VASP / VC exchange (uncharacteristic onramp)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: A customer takes out a HELOC, home equity loan, or second mortgage and uses the proceeds to purchase virtual currency or wires the proceeds to a VASP for the purchase of virtual currency.
indicators.red_flag: Home-equity/loan proceeds → VC purchase / wire-to-VASP (leveraged scam funding)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D3 (Wire / ACH / EFT & cross-border payment data (incl. EMT, P2P, remittance)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer receives what appears to be a deposit of virtual currency from a virtual currency address at or slightly above the amount that the customer previously transferred out of their virtual currency account.  This deposit is then followed by outgoing transfers from the customer in substantially larger amounts.
indicators.red_flag: Small VC return-deposit → escalating outbound transfers (fake-payout bait-and-escalate)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Accounts with large balances that are inactive or have limited activity begin to show constant, uncharacteristic, sudden, abnormally frequent, or significant withdrawals of large amounts of money being transferred to a VASP or being exchanged for virtual currency.
indicators.red_flag: Dormant high-balance account → sustained large VASP/VC drawdown
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: A customer sends multiple electronic funds transfers (EFTs) or wire transfers to a VASP or sends part of their available balance from an account or wallet they maintain with a VASP and notes that the transaction is for “taxes,” “fees,” or “penalties.”
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer with a short history of conducting several small-value EFTs to a VASP abruptly stops sending EFTs and begins sending multiple high-value wire transfers to accounts of holding companies, limited liability corporations, and individuals with which the customer has no prior transaction history.
indicators.red_flag: Small VASP EFT trial run → high-value wires to no-relationship LLCs/individuals (trial-then-commit)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D3.

indicators.flag: System monitoring and logs show that a customer’s account is accessed repeatedly by unique IP addresses, device IDs, or geographies inconsistent with prior access patterns.  Additionally, logins to a customer’s online account at a VASP come from a variety of different device IDs and names inconsistent with the customer’s typical logins.
indicators.red_flag: Account access from inconsistent IP/device/geo (remote-control / account-takeover)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D9 (Identity-verification, document & device/session telemetry), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer mentions that they are transacting to invest in virtual currency using a service that has a website or application with poor spelling or grammatical structure, dubious customer testimonials, or a generally amateurish site design.
indicators.red_flag: VC investment via amateurish/low-quality site or app (fraudulent-platform OSINT)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: A customer mentions visiting a website or application that is purported to be associated with a legitimate VASP or business involved in investing in virtual currency.  The website or application shows warning signs such as a web address or domain name that is misspelled in such a manner as to resemble that of another business, a recently registered web address or domain name, no physical street address, international contact information, or contact methods that include only chat or email.
indicators.red_flag: Look-alike / newly-registered VASP domain, no address, chat-only contact (spoofed-platform OSINT)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: A customer mentions that they downloaded an application on their phone directly from a third-party website, rather than from a well-known third-party application store or an application store installed by the manufacturer of the device.
indicators.red_flag: Sideloaded app from third-party site, not official store (malicious-app onboarding)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D9 (Identity-verification, document & device/session telemetry), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer receives a large amount of virtual currency such as ether at an exchange, subsequently converts the amount to a virtual currency with lower transaction fees such as TRX, and then abruptly sends it out of the exchange.
indicators.red_flag: Receive ETH → convert to low-fee VC (TRX) → abrupt off-exchange send (rapid chain-hop layering)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.
